cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Maps & Mapwork
cards.back: Geological maps show the distribution of rock types at the surface using colours and symbols

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Maps & Mapwork
cards.back: An outcrop is the area where a particular rock unit is exposed at the surface

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Maps & Mapwork
cards.back: Strike is the compass direction of a horizontal line on a dipping surface; dip is the angle and direction the surface slopes

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Maps & Mapwork
cards.back: The V-rule: dipping beds produce V-shaped outcrop patterns in valleys; the V points in the direction of dip for shallow dips

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Maps & Mapwork
cards.back: Unconformities on maps show as a boundary where younger rocks overlie eroded older rocks, representing a time gap

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Maps & Mapwork
cards.back: Cross-sections are drawn by projecting surface geology into the subsurface along a vertical plane

cards.front: What should you know about gcse geology exam tips — geological maps & mapwork?
cards.back: 1. For Geological Maps & Mapwork questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3. When interpreting data, consider the quality and limitations of the evidence 4. Apply your understanding of Geological Maps & Mapwork to fieldwork observations and map data 5. For evaluation, weigh competing geological theories with evidence
